title: Ratios & Rates
subtitle: Equivalent Ratios, Unit Rates, Percent
bounds: Counts 2-10 (a total <= 20). Every scale factor, unit rate, divisor and quotient 2-10; every x and ÷ a times-table fact; correct values whole numbers <= 100. Percents: 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 75, 80, 90; tens (50 included) on wholes 10q (q 2-9), 25%/75% on wholes 4q (q 2-10), 50% also on wholes 2q (q 2-10). Sharing by a ratio: terms 2-8 summing to <= 10. Ratio answers p:q with p, q <= 20. Distractors may be fractions or decimals (what the misreading gives).

tiers.name: Ratio Language
tiers.description: Write a ratio in the order asked: part to part, part to whole.

tiers.name: Equivalent Ratios
tiers.description: Scale both terms by the same number to fill the gap.

tiers.name: Unit Rates & Units
tiers.description: Find the rate for 1, and convert units with a rate.

tiers.name: Percent of a Number
tiers.description: Find 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% and tens of percent of a whole.

tiers.name: Parts, Wholes & Rates
tiers.description: Two steps: share a total by a ratio, find a whole from a percent, scale a price.

REVERSED.student: Order matters: write the first thing named first.
REVERSED.teacher: Writes the ratio terms in the opposite order (3:5 for blue to red = 5:3).

PART_TO_WHOLE.student: It asks part to part. Compare the two groups, not a group to the total.
PART_TO_WHOLE.teacher: Uses the total as one term of a part-to-part ratio.

PART_TO_PART.student: "To all" means the total. Add the groups to get the second number.
PART_TO_PART.teacher: Gives a part-to-part ratio when a part-to-whole ratio is asked.

WHOLE_FOR_PART.student: Take the known group away from the total first to get the other group.
WHOLE_FOR_PART.teacher: Uses the given total as the count of the remaining group.

ADDITIVE.student: Ratios grow by multiplying, not adding. Times both numbers by the same amount.
ADDITIVE.teacher: Adds the same amount to both terms instead of scaling (2:3 = 11:12).

WRONG_TERM.student: Multiply the number that matches, not the one you already have.
WRONG_TERM.teacher: Applies the scale factor to the given term instead of the missing one.

FACTOR_ONLY.student: That is only the first step. Use that number to finish.
FACTOR_ONLY.teacher: Stops at the scale factor or unit rate and gives it as the answer.

MULTIPLIED_RATE.student: Going to a bigger unit or finding per 1, divide. You multiplied.
MULTIPLIED_RATE.teacher: Multiplies the two quantities when the rate needs a division.

DIVIDED_RATE.student: Going to a smaller unit, there are more of them: multiply.
DIVIDED_RATE.teacher: Divides by the conversion rate when converting to the smaller unit.

INVERTED.student: Divided the wrong way. Per 1 means divide the total by the count.
INVERTED.teacher: Divides the count by the total, giving the reciprocal rate.

PERCENT_AS_PART.student: The percent is not the answer. Find that share of the whole.
PERCENT_AS_PART.teacher: Gives the percent itself as the part (25% of 40 = 25).

SUBTRACTED.student: Percent of means a share of the whole, not whole minus the percent.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the percent from the whole (25% of 40 = 15).

TENTH_FOR_ALL.student: Dividing by 10 gives 10%. Then scale it to the percent asked.

ONE_PART.student: That is one share (25% or 10%). Multiply by how many shares you need.
ONE_PART.teacher: Finds the unit share but does not scale to the percent or whole asked.

OTHER_PART.student: Check what it asks for: this group, the other group, or the whole.
OTHER_PART.teacher: Answers for the other group in the ratio.

PART_AS_TOTAL.student: The big number is the total of both groups. Split it into parts first.
PART_AS_TOTAL.teacher: Treats the given total as the count of one group.

PERCENT_OF_PART.student: This number IS the percent. The whole is bigger than it.
PERCENT_OF_PART.teacher: Takes the percent of the given part instead of finding the whole.

TOTAL_AS_UNIT.student: Find the price of 1 first: total price ÷ how many.
TOTAL_AS_UNIT.teacher: Multiplies the total price by the new count, skipping the unit rate.
